label: SpecRequirement
text: Each kind's status reports its lifecycle through a dedicated phase type, giving DenoJob, DenoPod, DenoRun, OpenBao-era workloads, PolicyEngine, PolicyWorkflowPod, PolicyWorkflowRun and RunTrigger a shared vocabulary of states that other code can switch on.

label: SpecRequirement
text: DenoPermissions.DenoSpec converts the CRD permission set into a denospec.Permissions value, copying the scalar flags directly and routing each per-resource permission through the DenoPermission converter; a nil receiver yields nil instead of panicking.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ServiceAccountRef.DenoSpec converts the reference into a denospec.ServiceAccountRef carrying Name and Namespace, and returns nil for a nil receiver so a missing service account stays distinguishable from an empty one.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The package registers one group/version and adds every custom kind (DenoJob, DenoPod, DenoRun, OpenBao, PolicyEngine, PolicyWorkflowPod, PolicyWorkflowRun, RunTrigger) to its scheme, so a controller can build a client for any of them.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Tests assert that a deep copy of a kind shares no backing storage with its original and that an absent service-account reference is distinguishable from a present but zero-valued one, since both properties are silent failures when they regress.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every custom kind pairs a Spec holding the desired state with a Status holding observed state, and ships a List companion, so controllers and clients can reconcile and enumerate each resource.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Permission, service-account, pod-template, exec-probe, restart-policy and concurrency-policy types live once in types_shared.go and are embedded by the workload kinds, so those shapes have a single definition that all kinds inherit.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every kind and list carries generated DeepCopyInto, DeepCopy and DeepCopyObject methods so it satisfies runtime.Object and can be cached by informers, and the copies must not alias any nested map, slice or pointer from the source object.

label: SpecRequirement
text: main builds the REST config with clientcmd.BuildConfigFromFlags from the kubeconfig path, exits 1 with a logged "loading kubeconfig" error when that fails, and passes the same host to the registry and the provider: the kubeconfig's server unless --host is set, in which case the flag wins.

label: SpecRequirement
text: envOr answers the environment variable when it is non-empty and the fallback otherwise, and envOrInt64 answers the parsed base-10 64-bit value when the variable is non-empty and parses, otherwise the fallback; both feed flag defaults so an unset or unparseable variable never overrides the compiled-in value.

label: SpecRequirement
text: main runs providerImpl.Run under a context cancelled by SIGINT or SIGTERM and exits with status 1 after logging "provider stopped" if Run returns an error.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The package provides one main function that acts as the provider process entrypoint, declares a config struct for its settings, and holds no reconcile logic; the remaining behaviour lives in the helpers envOr, envOrInt64, defaultRunTTL, caData and readIfSet.

label: SpecRequirement
text: main sets KUBE_FEATURE_WatchListClient to false before any client-go call, because kcp's APIExport virtual workspace sends no bookmark and an informer's initial list would otherwise never complete, leaving a provider that looks healthy and reconciles nothing.

label: SpecRequirement
text: main writes "deno-kcp-provider: --kubeconfig or KUBECONFIG is required" to stderr and exits with status 2 when the kubeconfig setting is empty.

label: SpecRequirement
text: readIfSet returns nil for an empty path, and for a path it cannot read it logs a warning naming the path and returns nil rather than failing startup, so a mistyped CA path surfaces as failed TLS verification instead of a provider that will not start.

label: SpecRequirement
text: When --bundled-actions-dir is empty, main derives it as the policy engine directory joined with "/../policies/gha-lite/bundled-actions" rather than leaving it unset.

label: SpecRequirement
text: defaultRunTTL answers nil for a negative seconds value, which disables the default run TTL, and otherwise returns a pointer to a copy of the value, which main passes on as DefaultRunTTLSeconds.

label: SpecRequirement
text: caData returns the REST config's CAData when it is non-empty, otherwise the contents of CAFile when that file reads successfully, otherwise nil.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The exec pod runner's TrustBundle is a closure that returns caData(restCfg) while the provider is still nil and providerImpl.TrustBundle() once it exists, because the OpenBao root CA does not exist until a namespace has asked for a certificate and the provider that generates it is built from this runner.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every setting is a flag whose default is the environment variable and then a fixed fallback, in the order flag, then environment, then default: --kubeconfig (KUBECONFIG, empty), --host (KCP_HOST, empty), --runs-dir (RUNS_DIR, "runs"), --policy-engine-dir (POLICY_ENGINE_DIR, "../policy-engine/lib/policy-engine-server-gha-lite"), --bundled-actions-dir (BUNDLED_ACTIONS_DIR, empty), --deno-bin (DENO_BIN, "deno"), --pod-timeout (no environment variable, 5m), --token-ttl (no environment variable, 1h), --metrics-listen (METRICS_LISTEN, empty, disabling the endpoint), --run-ttl-seconds (RUN_TTL_SECONDS, 3600, negative disables), --write-status (no environment variable, true), --service-domain (KCP_SERVICE_DOMAIN, "kcp.local"), --openbao-addr (OPENBAO_ADDR, empty), --openbao-token (OPENBAO_TOKEN, empty), --openbao-ca-cert (OPENBAO_CACERT, empty), --openbao-mount (OPENBAO_MOUNT, "pki"), --openbao-role (OPENBAO_ROLE, "denopod"), --openbao-intermediate-ttl (OPENBAO_INTERMEDIATE_TTL, "43800h") and --openbao-leaf-ttl (OPENBAO_LEAF_TTL, "720h").

label: SpecRequirement
text: main builds the registry with provider.NewRegistry, the engine runner with execrunner.NewEngine, the exec pod runner with execrunner.NewPod, and then the provider with provider.New, passing the registry as runtime and minter and the pod and engine runners in; each failure logs its own message ("building registry", "building engine runner", "building exec pod runner", "building provider") and exits with status 1.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every conversion method is nil-safe: a nil DenoPermissions, DenoPermission or ServiceAccountRef receiver returns a nil pointer instead of dereferencing it, so an unset field in the custom resource becomes an unset field in the deno spec and an omitted class never blocks the whole conversion.

label: SpecRequirement
text: External source trees the build depends on are declared in .gitmodules and the Go module graph in go.mod with go.sum, so a checkout pins the exact upstream revisions this repository was built against.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The repository keeps the operator-facing how-tos that back the KCP integration: local KCP development in docs/KCP_DEV_HOW_TO.md, the policy engine's KCP wiring in docs/POLICY_ENGINE_KCP.md with its how-to in docs/POLICY_ENGINE_HOW_TO.md, the OpenBao PKI path in docs/OPENBAO_PKI.md, and the runtime and embedding research notes in docs/DENO_RUNTIME_KCP.md and docs/DENO_EMBEDDING_RESEARCH.md.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The Makefile remains the single build entrypoint for the repository's targets, so generated artifacts and controller builds are produced the same way by every contributor.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ServiceAccountRef.DenoSpec forwards the reference's name and namespace into denospec.ServiceAccountRef, so the identity a run executes under survives the trip from the custom resource to the deno spec.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The decisions that shape the run path stay recorded as accepted ADRs: cancelling policy workflow runs in docs/adrs/0001-cancel-policy-workflow-runs.md, native run admission in docs/adrs/0002-native-run-admission.md, and the event-driven reconcile loop in docs/adrs/0003-event-driven-reconcile-loop.md, so a change to reconcile, admission or cancellation is argued against the recorded decision rather than re-litigated.

label: SpecRequirement
text: DenoPermission.denoSpec maps one permission class onto denospec.Permission, forwarding allow, allowList, deny and denyList so an operator can restrict a class by denylist, allowlist or boolean as the CRD declares.

label: SpecRequirement
text: DenoPermissions.DenoSpec converts the custom-resource permission block into a denospec.Permissions value, carrying the all, noPrompt, hrTime and allowScripts scalars through unchanged and filling each per-class slot (read, write, net, env, run, ffi, sys, import, ignoreEnv) from that class's own DenoPermission.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The .tools/open-architecture/validate.py check_values pass keeps the manifests consistent with the Go types: KIND_MANIFESTS maps each sc.kind.* id to its schema file and APIEXPORTS maps denoruntime and policyworkflowruns to their export files, then the upstream api.short is compared against names.shortNames[0], api.resource against names.plural, and the upstream phase and condition lists against the Go Phase and Condition constants, reporting an error for each pair that differs.

label: SpecRequirement
text: APIExport denoruntime lists seven resources in group deno.computer with the schema reference carried per entry: denopods to v1alpha1-3.denopods.deno.computer, denoruns to v1alpha1-2.denoruns.deno.computer, denojobs to v1alpha1-4.denojobs.deno.computer, runtriggers to v1alpha1-3.runtriggers.deno.computer, policyengines to v1alpha1-2.policyengines.deno.computer, policyworkflowpods to v1alpha1-5.policyworkflowpods.deno.computer and openbaos to v1alpha1-1.openbaos.deno.computer, so one export publishes the whole runtime chain.

label: SpecRequirement
text: APIExport policyworkflowruns publishes the single policyworkflowruns resource in group deno.computer against schema v1alpha1-4.policyworkflowruns.deno.computer, so a workspace that only needs the direct run path binds this export instead of the denoruntime one.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each APIResourceSchema metadata.name is v1alpha1-N.<plural>.deno.computer with the index fixed per plural, not globally unique: openbaos 1, denoruns 2, policyengines 2, denopods 3, runtriggers 3, denojobs 4, policyworkflowruns 4, policyworkflowpods 5, so the APIExport schema references resolve to one schema each.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The shell helpers install-provider.sh, start-kcp.sh, start-openbao.sh, stop-kcp.sh, demo.sh and demo-deno-runtime.sh sit beside the manifests for bring-up, install, teardown and demos; they carry no schema and are not part of the manifest cross-check.

label: SpecRequirement
text: WorkspaceType denoruntime extends workflow and universal, both from path root, and declares two default API bindings at path root:deno-provider, policyworkflowruns first and denoruntime second, so a workspace of this type gets the direct run path and the whole runtime chain together.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Required spec fields are exactly DenoPod script, DenoRun script, DenoJob template, RunTrigger policyWorkflowPod and jobTemplate, PolicyWorkflowPod workflow and policyEngine, and OpenBao namespace; PolicyEngine and PolicyWorkflowRun declare no required spec field, so their spec may be empty.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every version enables subresources.status, so phase and conditions are written by the provider through the status subresource and not by the tenant through the main resource.

label: SpecRequirement
text: WorkspaceType workflow extends universal from path root and declares one default API binding, export policyworkflowruns at path root:deno-provider, so a workspace of this type can create PolicyWorkflowRun objects without an explicit binding.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each spec.names declares kind, listKind as the kind with List appended, plural, singular as the lowercased kind, and a one-element shortNames list: DenoPod denopods denopod dpod, DenoRun denoruns denorun drun, DenoJob denojobs denojob djob, RunTrigger runtriggers runtrigger rtrig, PolicyEngine policyengines policyengine peng, PolicyWorkflowPod policyworkflowpods policyworkflowpod pwpod, PolicyWorkflowRun policyworkflowruns policyworkflowrun pwr, OpenBao openbaos openbao obao; the short name is what the Go types carry as api.short and the plural is what they carry as api.resource.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every APIResourceSchema declares spec.group deno.computer, spec.scope Namespaced, and exactly one version named v1alpha1 with served and storage both true, so each kind is a namespaced tenant resource in one group at one stored version.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every kind's status carries a conditions array whose items are objects marked x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields, so a standard condition set can be attached without a schema change and the Condition constants the Go types declare stay expressible.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Status phase enums are fixed per kind and mirror the Go Phase constants: DenoPod, DenoRun and DenoJob use Pending, Running, Succeeded, Failed; RunTrigger uses Pending, Triggered, Skipped, Failed; PolicyEngine and PolicyWorkflowPod use Pending, Running, Failed; PolicyWorkflowRun adds Cancelled to the four-state set; OpenBao declares no phase and reports ready plus message instead.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The registry carries exactly one entry for each of the ten top-level manifests: deno-job.yaml, deno-pod.yaml, deno-run.yaml, native-fire-pod.yaml, openbao.yaml, openbao-tls-pod.yaml, policy-workflow-run.yaml, policyengine.yaml, policyworkflowpod.yaml and runtrigger.yaml.

label: SpecRequirement
text: policyworkflowpod.yaml instantiates Kind PolicyWorkflowPod, resource policyworkflowpods, and the registry checks it against policyworkflowpod-apiresourceschema.yaml.

label: SpecRequirement
text: policy-workflow-run.yaml instantiates Kind PolicyWorkflowRun, resource policyworkflowruns, and the registry checks it against policyworkflowrun-apiresourceschema.yaml.

label: SpecRequirement
text: deno-run.yaml instantiates Kind DenoRun, resource denoruns, and the registry checks it against denorun-apiresourceschema.yaml.

label: SpecRequirement
text: deno-pod.yaml instantiates Kind DenoPod, resource denopods, and the registry checks it against denopod-apiresourceschema.yaml.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The names returned by exampleFilesOnDisk agree with the File fields of exampleFiles, so adding or removing a manifest on disk without updating the registry fails the integration suite.

label: SpecRequirement
text: openbao.yaml instantiates Kind OpenBao, resource openbaos, and the registry checks it against openbao-apiresourceschema.yaml.

label: SpecRequirement
text: native-fire-pod.yaml also instantiates Kind DenoPod, resource denopods, against denopod-apiresourceschema.yaml, covering the same Kind with a different runtime path.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every manifest the registry names sits directly in the examples root with a .yaml extension, so a registry entry that points at a missing, renamed or non-YAML file is a lookup the disk walk never confirms.

label: SpecRequirement
text: exampleFilesOnDisk reads the examples root, skips every directory entry and every entry whose extension is not .yaml, and returns the remaining file names sorted.

label: SpecRequirement
text: runtrigger.yaml instantiates Kind RunTrigger, resource runtriggers, and the registry checks it against runtrigger-apiresourceschema.yaml.

label: SpecRequirement
text: deno-job.yaml instantiates Kind DenoJob, resource denojobs, and the registry checks it against denojob-apiresourceschema.yaml.

label: SpecRequirement
text: exampleByName returns the registry entry whose File matches the given name and reports true, and reports false with a zero example when no entry matches, so an unknown example is a lookup miss and not a zero value.

label: SpecRequirement
text: policyengine.yaml instantiates Kind PolicyEngine, resource policyengines, and the registry checks it against policyengine-apiresourceschema.yaml.

label: SpecRequirement
text: DenoPod is exercised by three separate top-level manifests (deno-pod.yaml, native-fire-pod.yaml, openbao-tls-pod.yaml), so one Kind is covered by more than one configuration.

label: SpecRequirement
text: exampleFiles returns the registry of example entries in a fixed order, and each entry carries File, Kind, Resource and Schema, so a consumer can pair a manifest name with the Kind it instantiates, the plural resource and the APIResourceSchema that describes it.

label: SpecRequirement
text: openbao-tls-pod.yaml also instantiates Kind DenoPod, resource denopods, against denopod-apiresourceschema.yaml, showing the pod wired to OpenBao over TLS.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The global workspace runs DenoPod plc with restartPolicy Always, the denopod.deno.computer/run finalizer, SERVICE_TLS true, port 2587, and a readiness probe that resolves plc.default.global.svc.kcp.local and requests /health, so the pod reports ready only when its own cluster-local name answers through the virtual DNS shim.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The example's live acceptance brings the whole market up in a throwaway state directory and exits non-zero unless every workload is up and reachable. It is bash with set -euo pipefail; ACCEPT_ROOT (default a fresh mktemp -d) is the one directory it owns, and an EXIT trap stops everything it started and removes that directory, never stopping or touching a kcp, kine or OpenBao it did not start. It asks the kernel for three free 127.0.0.1 ports, for kcp, kine and OpenBao, instead of pinning any, so it cannot collide with another instance on the machine. It starts kcp with ROOT under ACCEPT_ROOT and KCP_SECURE_PORT and KINE_ENDPOINT set to two of those ports through deploy/start-kcp.sh, installs the provider through deploy/install-provider.sh, builds ./cmd/deno-kcp-provider into ACCEPT_ROOT, starts OpenBao with OPENBAO_DIR under ACCEPT_ROOT and OPENBAO_LISTEN on the third port through deploy/start-openbao.sh, and runs the provider with --kubeconfig, --openbao-addr, --openbao-token root and RUNS_DIR under ACCEPT_ROOT. It then runs the example's apply.sh with ORG_ROOT the repository parent, KUBECONFIG the kcp admin kubeconfig, the same OPENBAO_LISTEN, START_OPENBAO=0, a bounded WAIT_SECONDS, and the key files under ACCEPT_ROOT. When apply.sh returns, whether it succeeded or not, it reads every DenoPod from kcp with kubectl and prints one line per check with its result and the decisive evidence: apply.sh exited 0; DenoPod plc in root:global, relay in root:relay, pds in root:alice, pds in root:bob and bidder in root:bob each reached phase Running and report ready true; DenoPod verifier in root:alice reached the terminal phase Succeeded; bob's pds answers on its own name, which the provider proves with its readiness probe through the shim and the host proves by fetching the same path from outside with curl against the host port; the bidder answers on its cluster-local name and on its host port. The host check names the scheme the listener actually speaks: the bob PDS serves TLS because its supervisor writes the injected leaf and appends the TLS flags, so its host check is https, and the bidder serves plain HTTP because its supervisor must not append those flags, so its host check is http; the provider's readiness probe is the one that does not care, because it tries https and then http. The five long-running pods are still Running with ready true when they are read a second time at least ten seconds later, so a pod that dies after startup fails the run. It prints a final table naming every check and its result, prints the tail of the provider log and the status of the failing pod when a check fails, and exits 0 only when every check passed.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The live acceptance must survive a provider that comes up, logs that it is waiting for its APIExport virtual workspace endpoints, and then reconciles nothing: every object apply.sh applies stays without a status and apply.sh fails on its first wait. After the provider is started and apply.sh returns, the acceptance must detect that state within a bounded window - no OpenBao object in any workspace carries status.ready true and no DenoPod exists in any workspace - and, when no workload exists yet, stop the provider, start it again, and run apply.sh again. It must make at least two and at most three attempts, print which attempt it is on, and record each attempt's apply.sh exit code. It must never restart the provider once a DenoPod exists, because the workloads are children of the provider and stopping it would orphan them.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The verifier's relay watch settles exactly once, with a 90 second timeout, closing the WebSocket on settle and reporting error or closed instead of hanging, so a relay that never emits the commit fails the pod within the timeout rather than holding it open forever.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The example creates a ServiceAccount named deno-runner in namespace default, a ClusterRole named deno-runner-read-pods granting get and list on deno.computer denopods, and a ClusterRoleBinding of that role to that ServiceAccount, and no other ClusterRole is added because that one already covers what every runner pod needs.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The alice workspace runs DenoPod verifier with restartPolicy Never, importing KCP_SHIM before anything else, creating an account on VERIFY_PDS, reading the returned DID back from VERIFY_PLC, making a first write so the PDS announces itself, then writing a second record while watching VERIFY_RELAY's subscribeRepos WebSocket, and exiting 0 only when plcStatus is 200, gotAccessJwt is yes and relaySawCommit is yes. A run that does not see its own commit on the relay fails.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The verifier treats relay frames as bytes, decoding ArrayBuffer and Blob payloads with TextDecoder before searching for its own DID, because the relay emits DRISL where a CBOR string is its bytes verbatim and a search over the raw frame would not find the DID.

label: SpecRequirement
text: README.md's service table adds root:bob DenoPod/pds (hono-pds, port 2585, pds.default.bob.svc.kcp.local) and root:bob DenoPod/bidder (hono-bidder, port 2586, bidder.default.bob.svc.kcp.local), its OpenBao table adds root:bob OpenBao/openbao bob.default, its prose says four workspaces, and its ceilings note that the bidder registers with an XRPC dispatcher, so it needs one reachable.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The service pods' supervisor script writes the injected KCP_CA_BUNDLE to ca.pem and sets DENO_CERT to it, writes KCP_TLS_CERT and KCP_TLS_KEY to tls.crt and tls.key and appends --tls-cert-file and --tls-key-file to the child argv, prepends KCP_SHIM to the Deno flags as --preload, spawns the entry module as a child process with stdin null and inherited stdio, and writes the child exitCode to result.json, so the child trusts the market CA and serves the injected leaf.

label: SpecRequirement
text: apply.sh applies 10-rbac.yaml in root:bob as it does in every workspace, and every DenoPod in bob names the deno-runner service account, so bob's pods read the objects they need under the same role as the other workspaces.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The alice workspace runs DenoPod pds under the deno-runner service account with restartPolicy Always, SERVICE_TLS true, --unstable-kv in SERVICE_DENO_FLAGS, port 2583, PDS_PUBLIC_HOSTNAME pds.default.alice.svc.kcp.local, PDS_PLC_DIRECTORY_URL pointed at the global PLC name, PDS_CRAWLERS pointed at https://127.0.0.1:2584, the listener address of the relay, and PDS_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX in SERVICE_ENV. The crawler URL is that address and not the cluster-local name of the relay because this pod is applied before the relay: the virtual DNS table is written once when the pod starts, so relay.default.relay.svc.kcp.local is not in it, the shim fails such a name with the message that it is not in the table and could not be discovered inside a catch that swallows it, and the PDS then never announces itself and the relay never carries this PDS's commits. A crawler URL that is an address needs no table lookup. The relay still reaches this PDS by the cluster-local name in PDS_PUBLIC_HOSTNAME, which is in the relay table because the relay starts after it.

label: SpecRequirement
text: apply.sh names the workspaces global relay alice bob, requires atproto-market/hono-bidder as well as hono-plc, hono-atproto-relay and hono-pds in its preflight check, generates a PDS key for bob and a key for the bidder, each distinct from alice's and each overridable by BOB_PDS_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX and BIDDER_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX, substitutes them into the manifests, applies bob's OpenBao authority with the other authorities, applies bob's PDS manifest before the bidder manifest, and reports the phase and readiness of both pds and bidder in its final summary.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every service pod's env allowList admits the shim's keys (SERVICE_*, KCP_SHIM, KCP_TLS_CERT, KCP_TLS_KEY, KCP_CA_BUNDLE, KCP_SERVICE_NAME, KCP_SERVICE_DOMAIN, KCP_DNS_TABLE, KCP_TOKENS, KCP_SERVER, KCP_NAMESPACE, PATH, HOME) and its write allowList admits only result.json, tls.crt, tls.key and ca.pem, with read and run allowed and noPrompt true, so the supervisor can write the material the shim injects and nothing else.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each workspace applies one OpenBao object named openbao in namespace default, carrying the finalizer openbao.deno.computer/namespace and naming the OpenBao namespace that serves it: global.default, relay.default, alice.default and bob.default respectively. The workspace's pods take their certificates from that authority and not from another workspace's.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The example creates exactly the four workspaces global, relay, alice and bob, each with spec.type.name denoruntime and spec.type.path root.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The relay workspace runs DenoPod relay with restartPolicy Always, SERVICE_TLS true, HOSTNAME relay.default.relay.svc.kcp.local on port 2584, and a readiness probe that resolves relay.default.relay.svc.kcp.local and requests /xrpc/_health.

label: SpecRequirement
text: apply.sh must not create the verifier after a fixed sleep. It must instead wait, with the same bounded WAIT_SECONDS deadline it uses elsewhere, until the peers the verifier reaches are observable - DenoPod pds in root:alice reports phase Running and ready true, which is the provider's own proof that pds.default.alice.svc.kcp.local resolves through the virtual DNS table and answers on /xrpc/_health - and only then apply the verifier manifest. When the deadline passes without that pod becoming ready, apply.sh must say so on stderr and still create the verifier, so the run reports the failure instead of hanging. A fixed sleep before a pod whose restartPolicy is Never is not a wait for anything and must not be written.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The live acceptance's EXIT trap must stop the workloads before it stops the provider that owns them. The DenoPod processes are children of the provider, so killing the provider orphans them and they keep holding the fixed host ports 2583 to 2587 of the example, which makes the next run on the same machine unable to bind them. The trap therefore deletes every DenoPod in every workspace through kcp first, waits, bounded, for the objects to disappear (the denopod.deno.computer/run finalizer is what stops each process, and it only runs while the provider is up), and only then stops the provider, OpenBao and kcp and removes ACCEPT_ROOT. It must not stop a process it did not start, and it must do this whether the checks passed or failed.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each configuration value comes from a flag that falls back to an environment variable: `-addr` from `BAOEMBED_ADDR` defaulting to `127.0.0.1:8200`, `-root-token` from `BAOEMBED_ROOT_TOKEN` defaulting to `root`, `-tls` from `BAOEMBED_TLS` compared to `1` and defaulting to off, and `-tls-dir` from `BAOEMBED_TLS_DIR` defaulting to empty, where an empty directory means a fresh temporary one.

label: SpecRequirement
text: In TLS mode the command uses the given TLS directory, or creates a fresh temporary directory when none is given, then calls `os.MkdirAll` on it with mode `0o700` because OpenBao refuses a certificate directory that does not exist; a failure to create the temporary directory writes `baoembed: making a certificate directory: %v` to stderr and exits with status 1, and a failure of `os.MkdirAll` writes `baoembed: making the certificate directory %s: %v` to stderr and exits with status 1.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A goroutine polls the configured address on a fixed interval rather than trusting an address the server reports, because dev mode is to be reached at the requested address, and the readiness line is emitted only once the embedded server answers there.

label: SpecRequirement
text: In TLS mode the command serves `https` and the readiness line carries the generated CA certificate path, formed by joining the TLS directory with `devTLSCAFile`; without TLS the scheme is `http` and the CA path is empty.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The command sets the environment variable `BAO_DEV_ROOT_TOKEN_ID` to the configured root token before starting the embedded server; if setting it fails, the command writes `baoembed: setting the root token: %v` to stderr and exits with status 1.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The package is a `main` package whose entry point `main` parses the command flags, starts the embedded OpenBao development server on the configured address, and holds it running instead of returning.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The command signals readiness by printing a line that begins with the constant `readyPrefix`, whose value is `"BAOEMBED "`, followed by the server URL built from the scheme and the configured address.

label: SpecRequirement
text: New fills in the Options fields the caller left unset: the Now clock falls back to time.Now and a zero DefaultBackoffLimit falls back to the package DefaultBackoffLimit, so a Reconciler built from a zero Options still decides against a real clock and a real retry limit.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The decider is a Reconciler value, and the only way to build one is New, which takes an Options value and returns a *Reconciler.

label: SpecRequirement
text: RunObservation reports one run by Name with its v1alpha1.DenoRunPhase in Phase, an optional exit code in ExitCode, a human-readable Message, and the run's outputs map in Outputs, so the decider can decide on a run without holding the v1alpha1.DenoRun itself.

label: SpecRequirement
text: denojob_test.go drives the decider by constructing Observed values and asserting directly on the returned Result, covering at least that a job with no runs yet creates exactly one run named demo-1 and reports DenoJobPending with Active one, and that the job reaches DenoJobSucceeded carrying its run's outputs with Succeeded one once that run reports DenoRunSucceeded.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Observed supplies the decoded observed state for one pass: the v1alpha1.DenoJob in Job, the slice of RunObservation for the runs the job owns in Runs, and the time the decision is made against in Now.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Reconciler.Reconcile takes a context.Context and an Observed snapshot and returns a Result plus an error; it performs no Kubernetes client work, so every effect the job needs is expressed in the returned Result for the caller to apply.

label: SpecInterface
name: Reconciler.Reconcile
signature: func (r *Reconciler) Reconcile(ctx context.Context, o Observed) (Result, error)

label: SpecRequirement
text: Result carries the complete plan for one pass: the DenoJobPhase in Phase, the observed run names in RunNames and the single run name in RunName, the runs to start in CreateRuns and the runs to stop in StopRuns, StartTime and CompletionTime, the Active, Ready, Succeeded, Failed and Retries counters, the ExitCode and Outputs of the selected run, the Conditions, the RequeueAfter delay, and the Delete flag for the runs together with the DeleteJob flag for the job.

intent: This context exists to pin down the deploy/examples/atproto/market example as an executable specification of what the kcp deno runtime must support: peer services that reach each other only by cluster-local name over TLS, with identity and certificates supplied from outside the pod. It is the reference topology that exercises workspace creation, per-workspace API bindings, per-workspace RBAC, per-workspace OpenBao authority selection, the provider's virtual DNS table and shim, and the TLS leaf injection path, so that a regression in any of those surfaces shows up as a failing verifier pod rather than as an untested assumption in the provider. The example also carries a live acceptance script, so that it is proven by bringing the whole topology up and reaching it, not only by decoding its manifests and fitting them to their schemas. Two properties of the provider virtual DNS shape the manifests: a workload address table is written once at pod start, so a consumer that starts before its producer cannot reach it by cluster-local name, and WebSocket construction cannot fall back to discovery at all. The PDS crawler therefore points at the relay listener address, which needs no table lookup, while the relay reaches the PDS by the cluster-local name its own later start puts in the table.
label: SpecContext
name: deploy-examples-atproto-market

intent: This context exists to describe the deployment manifests that register the deno.computer kinds with kcp and make them bindable by tenant workspaces. It states the fixed group, scope, version, naming and status shape every schema must carry, the resource membership of each APIExport, and the default API bindings each WorkspaceType applies, so the YAML stays a faithful, machine-checked mirror of the Go types rather than a hand-maintained duplicate.
label: SpecContext
name: deploy

intent: This context exists so the example manifests and the registry that describes them have a single written contract. The manifests are the only executable proof that each deno-kcp kind can be expressed as a Kubernetes object, and the registry is what lets the integration suite pair a manifest with its Kind, its plural Resource and its generated APIResourceSchema. Writing that pairing down makes drift detectable: a manifest added on disk without a registry entry, or a manifest whose kind stops matching the schema the registry names, is a spec violation rather than a silent gap in coverage.
label: SpecContext
name: deploy-examples

intent: The context exists to pin down the contract between the deno-kcp custom resources and the deno permission model they compile to, so that a DenoPod or policy-driven run gets exactly the permissions its spec asked for and nothing else. It also anchors the repo-level artifacts — module wiring, build entrypoint, and the ADRs and how-tos — that explain and reproduce how those resources are admitted, reconciled, and cancelled.
label: SpecContext
name: deno-kcp

intent: This context exists to pin down the provider's process boundary: the single main that turns operator input (flags and environment) into the registry, engine runner, pod runner and provider the controller needs, and the failure and shutdown behaviour around them. Everything else in the repository assumes a configured provider already exists; this context is what makes one.
label: SpecContext
name: cmd-deno-kcp-provider

intent: This context exists so that DenoJob reconciliation has one place that decides and no place that acts: internal/provider observes the cluster and writes the Result back, while internal/denojob only turns observed state into a plan. Splitting the decision out keeps the job's phase, counters, conditions, requeue delay and delete flags testable without a client, and lets the provider layer stay a thin observer and writer.
label: SpecContext
name: internal-denojob

intent: This context exists because the CRD types are the contract between the deno-kcp controllers and everything outside them: clients, informers and the denospec library all read these structs, so their field shape, phase vocabulary and deep-copy semantics must stay fixed and reviewable in one place. denospec.go is the bridge that keeps the Kubernetes-facing spelling of permissions and service accounts from drifting away from the library's own types.
label: SpecContext
name: api-v1alpha1

intent: This context exists so the repository can run a real OpenBao server from a single Go command with no external install, driven entirely by flags and environment variables. Integration tests and developers build and launch this binary, parse its readiness line to learn the URL and, in TLS mode, the generated CA path, then talk to the live server. The flag and environment surface, the root-token export, the TLS certificate directory handling, and the readiness line are therefore a contract that the tests depend on, and this document pins that contract.
label: SpecContext
name: internal-baoembed-cmd-baoembed
